task.description:
Hard gate: validate the test design for QRY-05, SBX-01, SBX-02, SBX-03.

Check:
1. Every MUST acceptance criterion has at least one runnable integration test
2. No SkipZigTest on any MUST-coverage test without a counterpart
3. Tests are self-contained (own fixtures, clean up)
4. Tests are wired into build.zig as test-integration-qry05-sbx
5. Test isolation respected (no shared mutable state between tests)
6. Known gap (SEC-MINOR-01 conflicting_agent_roles no audit) is documented as a known-gap test

Return PASS if all criteria met, FAIL with specific gaps.

result.summary: QRY-05 (6/6 tests) and SBX-01-03 (15/15 tests) are largely well-designed: no SkipZigTest, BPM_TEST_DB_URL required with clear error, per-test UUIDs, deferred cleanup, parameterised SQL, build.zig wired as test-integration-qry05-sbx, SEC-MINOR-01 gap documented as known-gap test (TC-SBX-01-04). FAIL on 1 BLOCKER + 2 MAJOR issues below.

issues.description: SBX-01 AC4 has no integration test. AC4 requires: GIVEN a caller bypasses the gateway and calls the service port directly with an implementer token (tenant_implementer role, no scope), WHEN handleSubmitTaskSpec executes, THEN HTTP 403 orchestrator_role_required is returned. The implAuth() helper is defined in sbx01_02_03_agent_role_gates_test.zig but is never used with handleSubmitTaskSpec — only with handleClaimSandbox (SBX-03 tests). TC-SBX-01-01 (scope-only) and TC-SBX-01-02 (orchestrator-role-only) do not cover this scenario because neither uses the implementer role credential. TEST-DESIGNER must add a TC-SBX-01-06 test: implAuth + handleSubmitTaskSpec → 403 orchestrator_role_required.

TC-QRY-05-06 spec title is 'Cross-tenant isolation' and the preconditions describe two distinct tenants (tenant A, tenant B), each with its own entity row. The implementation uses DEFAULT_TENANT_ID for both callers and tests two different users within the same tenant. The tenantAuth() helper is defined but unused in TC-06. Actual two-tenant isolation (same entity_key registered under two different tenant_ids, query issued with different tenant contexts) is not demonstrated. While no QRY-05 AC in requirements.yaml names cross-tenant explicitly, the spec case count is reported as 6 with TC-06 counted; if TC-06 is retired or renamed to 'user-grant isolation', the cross-tenant scenario remains unverified. TEST-DESIGNER should either rename TC-06 to reflect its true scope or add a genuinely two-tenant test using tenantAuth().

SBX-02 AC3 requires: GIVEN the same submission, WHEN spec_hash is computed over the server-authoritative principal (orch-a), THEN a client that pre-computed its hash over orch-b receives HTTP 409 spec_hash_mismatch on artifact submission. No test covers this 409 path. TC-SBX-02-03 verifies that two orchestrators with the same body produce different hashes, which indirectly confirms the hash is principal-bound, but it does not exercise the spec_hash_mismatch rejection. TEST-DESIGNER must add a test that submits a spec carrying a hash pre-computed over the wrong principal and asserts HTTP 409 spec_hash_mismatch; or, if the artifact-submission endpoint is out of scope for this handoff, document which test file will cover AC3 and gate TEST-RUNNER on that file being present.

SBX-02 AC6 states: 'The force-set runs before canonicalisation, so no code path hashes a client-supplied principal.' This is an implementation invariant. No test explicitly asserts it; it is only indirectly covered by TC-SBX-02-02 (discarded body principal) and TC-SBX-02-03 (hash differs per orchestrator). Consider adding a comment in TC-SBX-02-02 or a dedicated assertion that confirms the stored spec_hash matches a hash computed over the server-set principal, not the body value.

result.next_action: Route FAIL back to TEST-DESIGNER for rework (rework_count will become 1 of max 1). Required: add TC-SBX-01-06 (implAuth on handleSubmitTaskSpec), resolve TC-QRY-05-06 cross-tenant scope ambiguity, and address SBX-02 AC3 coverage.
